Test Description: Testing ability to optimize moves or scoring for a given game state and trying to have a grounded rule application
Difficulty Notes: Easy optimization problem with intuitive solution
Question: Assume: 1) no-inter player trading occurs, 2) there are no development cards left to draw, 3) in-hand VP cards count as points, 4) can use the combined Trade/Build phase, 5)For maritime trade, a city on a special harbor grants a 1:1 trade rate for its resource, while a city on a generic harbor grants a 3:2 trade rate for any resource. What is the maximum number of ore resource cards the green player can get by the end of the turn, given the player rolls a 12 in this turn? Return the answer in the following format: [prev_cards: <number of cards before this turn of that resource>, new_cards: <number of cards after the turn of that resource>]
Rationale: According to the given board state in the question, the green player has: 1 city at special harbour, and 3 settlements. The current resource pool of the green player is: [brick: 3, wool: 4, grain: 1, lumber: 3, ore: 3]. The development cards include: 1 road building, 1 year of plenty and 1 knight. Also has 3 knights already placed on the table. The total number of points the green player currently has is: 5 points (2 from city + 3 settlements). Since the player rolls a 12 in this turn, the green player gets: 3 wool resources. Making the new resource pool: [brick: 3, wool: 7, grain: 1, lumber: 3, ore: 3]. In order to get the maximum number of ore resource cards the green player can do the following: use the year of plenty resource card and gain 1 wool and 1 ore resource card (+1 ore resource). Use the maritime trade (2 wool for 1 any resource) * 2 (because city is located at the special harbor). So 8 wool would give 8 ores (by using maritime trade 4 times) (+8 ore cards). Therefore by the end f this turn the green player can get a maximum of 9 more ore cards.
